findings.description: The real EARS-001 text names exactly six live-price-dependent columns (price, market value, unrealized P&L, unrealized %, estimated unrealized tax, net unrealized). The real code has a SEVENTH formula column — `Quote Date` (POSITIONS_HEADER index 12) — built by `quote_date_formula()` as `=IFERROR(TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE("<ticker>","tradetime"))-DATE(1970,1,1),"0"),"")`, with an elaborate epoch-rebasing/locale-proof encoding whose entire purpose (feeding the marks read-back settle pass) is outside SHEET-FORMULA-001's stated scope. All three B-runs (B1, B2, B3) independently surface this extra formula column and its exact encoding contract; none of the three spec-only A-runs invent anything resembling it (they all stop at the spec's six named columns) — confirming this is genuine code-side surplus, not something the spec forces or even gestures at.

Code+tests pin exact formula algebra the spec never states: Market Value=`=E{r}*B{r}`, Unrealized P&L=`=F{r}-D{r}`, Est. Unrealized Tax=`=G{r}*H{r}`, Net Unrealized=`=G{r}*(1-H{r})`, Unrealized %=`=IF(D{r}=0,0,G{r}/D{r})`, Price=`=GOOGLEFINANCE("<ticker>","price")` (alias-resolved ticker, two-arg form). SHEET-FORMULA-001 says only 'as sheet formulas' — it specifies neither which sibling cells each formula reads nor the operator chain. B1/B2/B3 converge on identical column letters and formula shapes (matching `lib.rs` verbatim), while the three A-runs — writing from spec text alone — each invented a materially different formula shape (net_unrealized as `pnl-(pnl*rate)` vs `pnl-est_tax` vs `pnl*(1-rate)`; MAX-clamping negative tax in two of three runs but not the real code).

The zero-cost-basis tie-break for Unrealized % is pinned to a literal `0` (`=IF(D{r}=0,0,G{r}/D{r})`), never blank or an error. The spec is silent on this edge case entirely. Notably, the two A-runs that handled this case at all (A1, A2) both independently guessed empty-string `""` instead — an assumption artifact with no spec basis that also happens to disagree with the real code's constant, though since it isn't spec-traced it doesn't count as an A-side finding, only underscores that this tie-break value is pure code-side surplus.

The Est. Tax Rate `Value` cell must be a percent-suffixed numeric string (e.g. `"20.0000%"`, produced by `fmt_ppm`) written via Sheets `userEnteredValue` (never forced `stringValue`), so it coerces to the numeric fraction the post-tax formulas (`=G*H`, `=G*(1-H)`) multiply directly — a load-bearing value-encoding/typing rule that the spec's bare phrase 'engine-written values' never specifies. Directly pinned by the dedicated test `est_tax_rate_cell_is_numeric_percent_the_posttax_formulas_can_multiply` and the `SheetsViewClient::batch_update_view` doc contract; unanimous across B1-B3.

Row-anchoring invariant: every per-row formula must reference only that row's own 1-based row number and must never contain any other data row's row reference — explicitly tested in `per_row_formulas_reference_their_own_row_beneath_frozen_header` (asserts no 'leaked' cross-row references). This anti-mispairing guarantee is entirely unstated in SHEET-FORMULA-001, which only distinguishes formula columns from value columns, not row-addressing discipline. Unanimous across B1-B3.

A whole-tab 'zero formula cells' invariant for Open Lots, Realized, and both Tax bands (accrual + reserve-summary), tested explicitly in `tax_tab_is_kernel_exact_not_live_formula` — every cell in every row of three tabs/bands must be `Cell::Value`. The spec text operates at column granularity ('all other columns... as engine-written values') within the implicit context of one tab; the code+tests generalize this into an explicit multi-tab guarantee that spec text never names those tabs to extend the rule to.

Defensive `Err(ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow(symbol))` path: if `Snapshot.positions` ever yields two rows for the same symbol, `render_positions` refuses to emit ambiguous rows and errors instead. Grounded directly in `lib.rs` (marked as a structurally-unreachable-but-kept defensive assertion). Surfaced by B1 and B2 but conspicuously omitted by B3 — a genuine within-direction disagreement, though the finding itself is real and entirely unstated by the spec.

notes:
Direction A produced no findings that clear the bar (spec-traced behavior absent from the real code): SHEET-FORMULA-001's terse two-clause text (six named formula columns; everything else a value) is fully honored by the real code, so there is nothing for A to catch the code missing. The three A-runs do converge tightly on that essential structural answer (same six columns as Formula, rest as Value — medium-to-high agreement on the load-bearing question) but diverge sharply and non-unanimously on incidental implementation choices the spec is silent on (MAX-clamping negative unrealized tax in A2/A3 only, IFERROR-wrapping GOOGLEFINANCE/division in A3 only, empty-string vs later-observed-0 zero-basis tie-break, cents-vs-dollars unit handling, column letter assignments). Per the classification rules, none of these divergent inventions trace to explicit spec text, so they are assumption artifacts, not A-side findings — hence 'medium' rather than 'low' aAgreement (the core answer is stable; the incidental details are not, but incidental instability isn't itself a finding).

Direction B is highly stable and substantive: B1/B2/B3 converge on the extra Quote Date formula column, the exact per-column formula text and cell-reference algebra, the zero-basis tie-break constant, the percent-string/userEnteredValue tax-rate encoding, the row-anchoring invariant, and the whole-tab value-only invariant for Open Lots/Realized/Tax. The single inconsistency is B3's omission of the DuplicateSymbolRow guard (present in B1/B2) — a minor gap in an otherwise near-unanimous set of runs, hence 'high' rather than a perfect score.

Net relationship: real code (plus its tests) contains substantial machinery, encoding rules, invariants, and even an entire extra live-formula column that the terse EARS-001 text never states or implies — pure code-side surplus with no counterpart gap on the spec side. That asymmetry is exactly B-ONLY-DRIFT.
